[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SCA-2.7.10.md#abb-context]

### ABB Context

- **Parent L2 Capability**: Application Security Testing — [GUID-SEC-APP-CAP-DESC-1.7.02](../GUID-SEC-APP-CAP-DESC-1.7.02.md)
- **ABB Catalog**: [GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-CAT-2.7.06](../GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-CAT-2.7.06.md)
- **Capability Statement**: The enterprise SHALL have an architectural capability to identify and track open-source and third-party software components within applications and assess their known vulnerability status and license obligations.
page_texts.4:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SCA-2.7.10.md#abb-scope]

### ABB Scope

**In Scope**:

- Architectural capability to enumerate direct and transitive third-party dependencies in application build manifests
- Matching of identified components against known vulnerability databases
- License identification and policy compliance for consumed dependencies
- Continuous monitoring for newly published vulnerabilities affecting in-use components

**Out of Scope**:

- First-party source code analysis (see GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SAST-2.7.07)
- Runtime dependency behavior monitoring (see GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-RTCON-2.7.14)
- SBOM generation and attestation (see GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SBOM-2.7.23, though SCA findings feed SBOM)
- Security controls, tool selection, or configuration baselines (`standards/security/`)

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SCA-2.7.10.md#core-principles]

### Core Principles

- SCA capability SHALL be applied to every application that includes third-party or open-source dependencies.
- SCA SHALL be integrated into the development pipeline to produce findings before code is merged.
- The capability SHALL support continuous monitoring — new vulnerability disclosures for already-deployed component versions SHALL trigger notification to responsible teams.
- License compliance findings SHALL be treated as blocking for components whose license terms are incompatible with enterprise distribution or usage obligations.
page_texts.8:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SCA-2.7.10.md#dependency-enumeration]

#### Dependency Enumeration

**Architectural intent**: Establish a complete, accurate inventory of all direct and transitive software components consumed by an application.

**Design guidance**:

- Enumeration SHALL cover both direct dependencies and the full transitive dependency graph.
- The capability SHOULD integrate with package manager manifests (e.g., lock files) for the most accurate component inventory.
- Results SHALL be traceable to specific application versions and pipeline runs.
page_texts.9:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SCA-2.7.10.md#vulnerability-assessment]

#### Vulnerability Assessment

**Architectural intent**: Identify which enumerated components have known vulnerabilities and communicate that risk to development teams.

**Design guidance**:

- Vulnerability matching SHALL use a maintained, up-to-date vulnerability database.
- Findings SHALL include severity, affected component version, and available remediation version where known.
- Findings above a defined severity SHOULD block pipeline promotion unless an approved exception exists.
page_texts.10:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SCA-2.7.10.md#continuous-monitoring]

#### Continuous Monitoring

**Architectural intent**: Ensure that vulnerability exposure from third-party components is detected promptly after new disclosures, not only at build time.

**Design guidance**:

- The capability SHALL monitor deployed application component inventories against newly published vulnerability disclosures.
- Notifications SHALL be routed to the team responsible for the affected application, based on application ownership metadata in the artifact registry. Routing to shared inboxes or unowned channels is an architectural anti-pattern.
page_texts.11:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SCA-2.7.10.md#vulnerability-response-architecture]

#### Vulnerability Response Architecture

**Architectural intent**: Ensure that vulnerability notifications drive timely, tracked remediation — not ignored alerts.

**Design guidance**:

- The SCA continuous monitoring capability SHALL produce structured notifications that include: affected application, affected component and version, CVE identifier, severity, and the artifact(s) in production that contain the vulnerable component.
- Severity-based response requirements SHALL be tiered, with higher severity findings requiring faster response than lower severity findings. Specific response windows and escalation thresholds SHALL be defined in a jointly governed operational agreement between Security Architecture, Platform Engineering, and Application Development leadership.
- Escalation paths for non-response SHALL be defined in the enterprise vulnerability management process, jointly governed by Security Architecture, Application Domain, and the Architecture Governance body. Persistent non-response SHOULD result in the application being flagged as non-compliant in the enterprise application inventory.
- The architecture SHALL NOT rely on notification alone. The vulnerability management workflow SHALL include a periodic posture review (cadence defined by Security Architecture) that surfaces unresolved findings across the application estate, independent of per-event notifications.
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SCA-2.7.10.md#integration-interfaces]

### Integration Interfaces

| Interface | Direction | Consuming ABB | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Build Manifest Input | Inbound | Application Build System | Dependency manifests and lock files |
| Vulnerability Database | Inbound | External/Internal Vulnerability Feed | Known CVE and advisory data |
| Findings Output | Outbound | GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-CAT-2.7.06 | Structured findings for gate logic and tracking |
| SBOM Feed | Outbound | GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SBOM-2.7.23 | Component inventory data consumed by SBOM generation |
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SCA-2.7.10.md#zero-trust-alignment-nist-sp-800-207]

### Zero Trust Alignment (NIST SP 800-207)

SCA advances the Applications and Workloads pillar by ensuring the components that constitute a workload are known, assessed, and free of exploitable vulnerabilities before the workload is trusted with access to enterprise resources.
page_texts.14:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SCA-2.7.10.md#nist-sp-800-53-intent-alignment]

### NIST SP 800-53 Intent Alignment

This ABB enables the architectural intent of the SA family (supply chain risk management and component acquisition) and the SI family (flaw identification in software components). It also supports the intent of the RA (Risk Assessment) family for component-level risk evaluation.
page_texts.15:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SCA-2.7.10.md#constraints-and-dependencies]

### Constraints and Dependencies

- Effectiveness depends on the currency and coverage of the vulnerability database used; architecture must account for database latency in newly published advisories.
- SCA and SBOM (GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SBOM-2.7.23) are complementary; SCA provides vulnerability assessment while SBOM provides attestable inventory — both are needed for a complete supply chain security posture.
- Transitive dependency graphs can be large; pipeline performance implications must be considered in architecture decisions.
